q: An accused is denied production before a magistrate during a war Emergency, the officer citing the Proclamation. Which statement is correct?
options: The denial is unlawful, the liberty guarantee surviving every Proclamation
The denial is lawful, the Proclamation suspending the guarantee automatically
The denial is lawful if the detention relates to the conduct of the war
The denial is unlawful only where the detention exceeds ninety days
expl: The liberty guarantee is beyond suspension in any Emergency.
why: The third option offers a nexus test, which sounds principled and has no application to these two articles.
trapnote: No nexus argument can reach the two protected articles. They are outside suspension entirely.

q: A retrospective penal provision is enacted during a Proclamation of Emergency. Which statement is correct?
options: It is valid, the protection standing suspended for the duration of the Proclamation
It is valid if a Presidential order suspending remedies has been issued
It is void only where the punishment prescribed exceeds seven years
It is void, the protection against retrospective conviction being beyond suspension
expl: The protection against ex post facto conviction cannot be suspended.
why: The third option confuses suspension of a remedy with the survival of the substantive protection.
trapnote: Both protected articles remain substantively effective even where remedies elsewhere are suspended.

q: The 2023 reservation amendment is cited to claim that the term of the House has been extended. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: the amendment extended the term pending a census
The citation fails: the amendment reduced the term of the House to four years
The citation fails: term extension arises under the Emergency provisions alone
The citation succeeds where the census has not been completed in time
expl: Term extension is an Emergency consequence and has nothing to do with the reservation amendment.
why: The fourth option ties the two together through the census condition, which is the natural but wrong link.
trapnote: The census condition governs when a reservation operates, not how long a House lasts.

q: Consider the criminal procedure statute in force from July 2024 during President's Rule: 1-Its safeguards continue to operate. 2-They are suspended for the duration. 3-Their operation depends on a Presidential order. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
None of them
expl: Only safeguards-continue is true; suspension and order-dependence are both false, matching no listed pair.
why: The presence of a none option changes the arithmetic, and here exactly one statement survives.
trapnote: President's Rule changes who governs the State. It does not alter the criminal procedure statute.

q: Following the creation of twenty-six districts in 2022, President's Rule is imposed in the State. Which statement is correct?
options: The districts continue; only the political executive is displaced
The districts revert to their pre-2022 boundaries during the proclamation
The districts continue, but all local bodies stand dissolved automatically
The districts continue, and the High Court's jurisdiction stands suspended
expl: Administrative units and courts are unaffected; the political executive is displaced.
why: The third and fourth options each add a consequence that does not follow from the proclamation.
trapnote: President's Rule displaces the political executive. Administration and courts continue.

q: The November 2022 ruling is cited during an Emergency to justify denying bail hearings. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: the ruling permitted suspension of procedural rights
The citation fails: the ruling concerned President's Rule and not reservation
The citation succeeds where the Proclamation rests on armed rebellion
The citation fails: that ruling concerned reservation and not criminal procedure
expl: The ruling concerned the economic reservation and has no bearing on criminal procedure.
why: The third option misdescribes the subject-matter in a different direction, which tests precision rather than recall.
trapnote: Identify what the cited ruling actually decided before assessing whether it supports the proposition.

q: The 2024 ruling on community resources is cited to justify a retrospective penal provision during an Emergency. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation fails on one count: the protection is suspendable but the subject differs
The citation succeeds: the ruling permitted retrospective economic measures
The citation fails on two counts: wrong subject-matter and a non-suspendable protection
The citation fails on one count: the subject matches but the ruling was overruled
expl: The ruling concerned property and directives, and the protection cannot be suspended in any event.
why: Two options identify a single defect, so a candidate who stops at the first error selects a near miss.
trapnote: Where a citation fails for more than one reason, the option naming both is the complete answer.

q: Consider the position of the Election Commission in relation to President's Rule: 1-Its certificate is needed for extension beyond one year. 2-It conducts elections to the State Assembly thereafter. 3-Its certificate is needed for the original proclamation. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The certificate belongs to the extension stage, not the proclamation stage.
why: The third statement transplants a genuine requirement to the wrong stage, which is the standard construction here.
trapnote: Stage transplant: a real requirement moved one step earlier or later in the sequence.

q: A claim is made that the safeguards for night arrest of women stand suspended during a Proclamation of Emergency. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim fails: they are statutory safeguards unaffected by the Proclamation
The claim succeeds: all procedural safeguards yield during a Proclamation
The claim succeeds where a Presidential order suspending remedies has issued
The claim fails: they are suspended only where the ground is armed rebellion
expl: Statutory safeguards continue; a Proclamation does not repeal the criminal procedure statute.
why: The third option is the strongest distractor because such an order does affect access to courts for some rights.
trapnote: A suspension order affects remedies for specified rights. It does not repeal statutory procedure.

q: Consider Andhra Pradesh in January 1973: 1-President's Rule was imposed. 2-The Six-Point Formula followed later that year. 3-The resulting amendment inserted special provisions for the State. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three steps occurred in sequence during 1973.
why: The sequence runs from crisis to settlement to constitutional entrenchment, which is the pattern worth retaining.
trapnote: Crisis, settlement, entrenchment. The amendment came after the Formula, never before it.
